## Less work every second, same screen

This release cuts per-second overhead in the network path and in the dashboard. Nothing about what is measured or shown changes.

**Dashboard.** Rows whose text did not change are no longer rewritten. A steady "0 B/s" or an idle CPU used to touch every binding once a second; now a row whose label, value, gauge state and severity are identical is left alone, and a panel recomputes its visibility only when it changes.

**Linux.** Reading `/proc/net/dev` no longer allocates a string per counter. Only the two byte counters are parsed; the remaining fields are counted to keep the sixteen-field shape check. The only allocation per interface is its name.

**Windows.** Enumerating the network adapters no longer happens every second. The filtered adapter list is reused for thirty seconds and invalidated at once by the operating system's own network-change notification, so a cable pulled or a Wi-Fi dropped is picked up on the next round. The per-second counters are still read live on every round. A first enumeration that fails reads as a failure, not as a machine with no interfaces.

**Tests.** Five regression tests pin the new behaviour: an empty interface name and a counter past the 64-bit range are skipped, DOS line endings parse, the Windows provider answers consistently across two reads, and its off-Windows branch stays a clean false.
